text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a 12h overnight perf sweep on the kv-cache/alloc changes. TL;DR: OOMs dropped ~78% on the large-chat workload, but p99 token latency bumped ~3.2% and CPU syscall noise increased. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/test-runs/6752
perf-bot: nightly-perf-run 6752 completed in 11h34m — summary attached (errors: 3, OOMs: 2 -> 0 after knob changes)
aj: Can you paste the exact knob set you ran? also which model & batch profile?
maria: Ran on dedicated cluster w/ rtx-a100-40GB, model: redwood-7b-v2-fp16, batching profile: convo-heavy (avg seq 1024, burst 512). Knobs applied at runtime via env: 
```
EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=1
MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB=64
GARBAGE_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD=0.7
```
Result: OOMs down, memory fragmentation metric (allocator.fragmentation_ratio) fell from 0.58 -> 0.23, but tail latency up.
kevin: Interesting — that matches fragmentation reduction with smaller splits. But expandable_segments can increase the number of free-list ops and kernel call overhead; might explain the p99 blip. Did you capture allocator op counts?
maria: I grabbed allocator counters and a short flame graph. allocator.ops.free=1.2M, allocator.ops.alloc=1.8M, avg free-list length increased slightly. Flame: https://perf.redwood/flame/6752 (shows spike in cudaMalloc/cuMemFree around batching boundary).
sasha: Two quick thoughts: 1) max_split_size_mb=64 causes more splits which reduces internal waste but increases bookkeeping. 2) gc_threshold=0.7 delays aggressive GC — that can reduce churn but raise transient working set. Try gc_threshold=0.6 and track peak_resident_bytes.
luca: Also recall we changed kernel-routing last week (route-v3) which changed batch packing; could be the combo (more small allocations during autobalance). Suggest running with route-v2 + knobs to isolate.
aj: So propose A/B: A = (expandable=1, max_split=64, gc=0.7, route-v3) B = (expandable=0, max_split=128, gc=0.6, route-v2). Run both on identical traffic for 6h and compare OOMs, p99, and allocator.fragmentation_ratio.
kevin: +1. Also log: allocator.stats.{free_bytes,allocated_bytes,fragmentation_ratio,alloc_calls,free_calls}. We should ingest into graphite.
maria: I'll spin up experiments. Deployment command I'll use (from staging deploy helper):
```
/deploy perf/kv-alloc-experiment --env=dedicated --branches=route-v3:perf-alloc-v1 --knobs "expandable_segments=1,max_split_size_mb=64,garbage_collection_threshold=0.7"
```
deploy-bot: queued deploy perf/kv-alloc-experiment to cluster dedicated-5 (run-id: 2026-03-18-01).
sasha: For observability, add these runtime counters to the trace span and emit a heatmap per shard every 10m. Also capture kv-cache hit-rate per prefix length (0-64,65-256,>256).
maria: Will do. I'll also run a microbenchmark to measure overhead of expandable_segments toggle using synthetic alloc/free pattern. If overhead >1.5% in user CPU we revert.
aj: One minor ask — record the kernel batch size histogram (we suspect more small kernels). If the median kernel size drops that's telling.
luca: If route-v3 is the culprit, we could change batching heuristic to prefer consolidating short sequences for the same session (cheap), instead of spreading them across kernels. But that's more invasive. Let's see A/B first.
kevin: Sidenote: try setting MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB=96 as a middle ground if 64 causes too much overhead.
maria: Noted. I'll run A/B and a 3rd arm with split=96. Planning runtime: start at 02:00 UTC, 6h per arm, traffic sampled from prod shadow (2%). Will post consolidated CSV with columns: arm,oom_count,p99_ms,median_ms,fragmentation_ratio,alloc_calls,free_calls,peak_rss.
aj: Perfect. Also include a short reproduction snippet for the microbenchmark (paste to the thread once ready).
maria: Quick repro script (py pseudo):
```
# alloc microbench
for iter in range(1_000_000):
    t = torch.empty((rand_len,), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda')
    del t
```
I'll add synced barrier to mimic batching boundaries.
sasha: Great. One more: set garbage_collection_threshold to 0.65 in the 3rd arm instead of 0.7. small tweak.
maria: ok running variants: A(route-v3,64,0.7), B(route-v2,128,0.6), C(route-v3,96,0.65). Kickoff 02:00 UTC. Will report back with metrics + short notes. :thumbsup:
aj: Thanks! ping @kevin @sasha when you have csv.
kevin: thanks, will watch graphs.
perf-bot: perf alert — small regression flagged on p99 for run 6752 (delta +3.2%) — investigating.
